actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: Task 1 teleoperates a mobile dual-arm Franka FR3 platform with Robotiq 2F-85 grippers on a planar-drive base with a vertical spine to route a deformable cable across a fixture board
Everything runs in a single MuJoCo process (main.py): robot, cable, board and physics live in one simulation
The scene is the MuJoCo model full_robot_board_cable_routing
The model uses the implicitfast integrator with timestep 0.0005 s
The scene activates the mujoco.elasticity.cable plugin
The scene contains a cable composite with count 71 1 1 and initial none, described by its comment as 71 segments
The cable initialization writes four qpos values at each cable segment's ball joint

The actuator block declares a spine position actuator with ctrlrange 0 to 0.85, three base velocity actuators with ctrlrange -2.0 to 2.0 and -4.0 to 4.0, seven velocity actuators per FR3 arm with ctrlrange -8 to 8, -10 to 10 and -12 to 12, a position actuator per Robotiq gripper with ctrlrange 0 to 0.8, caster and TMRV steer actuators with ctrlrange -3.14159 to 3.14159, and roll and drive actuators with ctrlrange -80 to 80
The model has a home keyframe named home
TeleopSession is described as everything the input methods share and it owns the model and data
TeleopSession loads the scene with scene.load_model and constructs mujoco.MjData from the model
TeleopSession resets to the home keyframe when that key exists with mj_resetDataKeyframe and then calls mj_forward
TeleopSession.step_once advances the physics with mujoco.mj_step
scene.load_model loads the scene XML with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one initial state; the bridge takes no seed input and cap.world.reset.v1 restores model defaults, so a run repeats exactly on the same engine but no seed selects a different state

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the scene's explicitly declared joints, actuators, ctrlranges and timestep but integrates a placeholder motion (a velocity actuator sets its joint velocity to the control value and a position actuator moves a fixed fraction toward it); it resolves no contact, friction, equality, tendon, actuator gain, sensor or noise model

the 71-count composite cable with initial none is counted but not expanded; MuJoCo generates its 70 segment bodies and 69 ball joints at compile time (4 qpos and 3 qvel each, scene.py:113-121), so the real model's arrays are 315 qpos and 246 qvel, while the fake exposes only the 39 explicitly declared joints

cap.world.reset.v1 runs mj_resetData + mj_forward (the bridge contract), not the upstream home keyframe, cable layout, arm ready pose or spawn placement (session.py:53-57); the fake also zeroes the arrays instead of resolving qpos0
the upstream grasp servo, clip guide, cable speed cap and cable plugin applied by step_once are not applied; only the bridge's mj_step loop is served
no rendering, camera or image stream is exposed, and the keyboard, gamepad, VR and ROS 2 teleoperation layers of the benchmark are not served
snapshot and restore use the bridge's fallback copy of time/qpos/qvel/act/ctrl; the stand-in has no mj_getState/mj_setState, so this is not an exact integration-state snapshot
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine and the real-engine backend (sim) was not run
no physical robot is modelled or driven and no hardware run is claimed

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
